---
title: "Migrating from Shiny to RDesk"
format: html
---

If you are accustomed to building applications with Shiny, this guide will help you translate your mental model to RDesk's native desktop paradigm.

## Key Differences at a Glance

::: {#tbl-comparison}

| Concept | Shiny | RDesk |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Networking** | Requires HTTP server & WebSockets on local port | Zero network ports (Pure OS pipe IPC) |
| **UI Architecture** | R DSL (`fluidPage`, `tags$div`, `bslib`) | Modern HTML5/CSS3/JS (`www/`) |
| **Execution Paradigm** | Reactive dependency graph (`reactiveVal`, `observeEvent`) | Direct event-driven messaging (`app$on_message`) |
| **Distribution** | Requires R runtime installed or server host | Bundles standalone `.exe` with embedded R |
| **File Access** | Browser sandboxed file uploads/downloads | Native Windows file dialogs & direct filesystem access |

Comparison of Shiny and RDesk core features.
:::

## Mental Model Translation

### 1. The Reactive Graph vs. Event Handlers

In Shiny, changes ripple through a reactive graph:

```r
# Shiny
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  filtered_data <- reactive({
    data[data$cyl == input$cyl, ]
  })
  
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    plot(filtered_data())
  })
}
```

In RDesk, communication is explicit and message-driven:

```r
# RDesk
init_handlers <- function(app) {
  app$on_message("filter_cyl", function(payload) {
    df <- data[data$cyl == payload$cyl, ]
    p  <- ggplot(df, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + geom_point()
    
    list(
      chart = rdesk_plot_to_base64(p),
      count = nrow(df)
    )
  })
}
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Why Explicit Messaging?
Explicit message routing gives you complete control over when computations run, prevents runaway reactive cascade cycles, and makes debugging straightforward.
:::

### 2. UI Layouts

In Shiny, you construct HTML using R functions:

```r
# Shiny UI
fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Sales Dashboard"),
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(selectInput("dept", "Department", choices = c("All", "HR", "Sales"))),
    mainPanel(plotOutput("distPlot"))
  )
)
```

In RDesk, you have full access to native HTML5 and CSS in `www/index.html`:

```html
<!-- RDesk www/index.html -->
<div class="dashboard-container">
  <aside class="sidebar">
    <label for="dept">Department</label>
    <select id="dept" onchange="rdesk.send('filter_dept', { dept: this.value })">
      <option value="All">All</option>
      <option value="HR">HR</option>
      <option value="Sales">Sales</option>
    </select>
  </aside>
  <main class="content">
    <img id="main-chart" src="" alt="Main Visualization" />
  </main>
</div>
```

You can use any frontend library or CSS framework (Bootstrap, Tailwind, Lucide Icons, Chart.js, D3) without needing R wrapper packages.
